results.title: The packed nonzero indicator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c>0$, $K=2^c$, $B=4K$, $F_q$, $D=(K-1)F_q$ be as in the masked-digit statement and $R=\sum_{t=0}^q\rho_tB^t$ with all $\rho_t<K$. Then Consequently, for $N\in\mathbb N$, $KN=(R+D)\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}(KF_q)$ holds if and only if $N=\sum_{t\le q}[\rho_t>0]B^t$, the packed nonzero indicator of $R$; no separate mask condition on $N$ is needed.

results.title: Soundness of the packed-history construction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be valid for $r$ registers with $m$ instructions, $1\le k\le r$ and $a\in\mathbb N^k$. If the formula of the packed-history construction of $p$ holds for some natural values of its fresh variables, with every macro read as its relation (masks as bit inclusion, bitAnd as bitwise conjunction, power as exponentiation, lt as strict inequality), then $p$ accepts $a$, and its accepting run has exactly $q$ steps.

results.title: Completeness of the packed-history construction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be valid for $r$ registers with $m$ instructions, $1\le k\le r$ and $a\in\mathbb N^k$. If $p$ accepts $a$, then the formula of the packed-history construction of $p$ holds for some natural values of its fresh variables, with every macro read as its relation.
